diagnostic_evidence.quote: We smoothly extend both function so that they are constant in the normal direction to the original boundary

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own parametrization x = X(s) + r(x)n(s) (with r < 0 in Ω and n̄ the outward normal per (eq:normal)) gives the closest boundary point X(s) = x − r(x)n(s), so a normal-constant extension must be ḡ(x) = g(x − r(x)n̄(x)) and f̄(x) = f(x − r(x)n̄(x)). Both (eq:gbar) and (eq:fbar) instead use x + r(x)n̄(x): for x ∈ Ω this evaluates the boundary datum g at a strictly interior point (in 1D on Ω = (−1,1), x = 1−δ gives ḡ(x) = g(1−2δ) instead of g(1)), so ḡ is not constant along normals; for x ∈ B\Ω it evaluates f at a point strictly outside Ω, where f is not defined, so f̄ is circular/ill-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x + r(x)n̄(x) by x − r(x)n̄(x) in (eq:gbar) and (eq:fbar) (equivalently ḡ(x) = g(X(s)) with X(s) = x − r(x)n(s)), making both extensions well defined and constant in the normal direction.
issues.overall_effect: The extended data ḡ and f̄ used in the right-hand sides of every method are not the claimed closest-point extensions; as written f̄ is undefined on B\Ω. Coercivity proofs are unaffected (they use g only symbolically), but the well-definedness of the discrete problems' data and accuracy statements tied to these extensions are unreliable.
issues.title: Sign error in the definitions of the extended data ḡ and f̄; the constructions are ill-defined as written
issues.why_classification: A single forced local sign correction, supported by the paper's own parametrization two lines earlier, restores the stated construction; no formal result or guarantee depends on the erroneous form.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof correctly derives a(u,u) = ∫_B D|∇(φu)|² + (D/ε²)(1−φ)u² dx, but then declares this 'identical, up to epsilon scaling, to DDM1' and concludes coercivity with respect to ‖u‖² = ∫_B φ|∇u|² + ε⁻²(1−φ)u² dx. The two gradient terms are inequivalent: |∇(φu)|² does not dominate φ|∇u|². Counterexample family: for the tanh phase field take u = w/φ with w smooth, supported where φ ∈ (δ/2, δ), oscillating at wavenumber k = 1/(εδ); then a(u,u) ≤ C(a²k²|S| + a²|S|/(ε²δ²)) while ‖u‖² ≥ c·a²k²|S|/δ, so a(u,u)/‖u‖² → 0 as δ → 0. Hence no coercivity constant c > 0 exists for the stated norm; DDM1's term-by-term argument does not carry over.

failure_location.quote: This is identical, up to epsilon scalling, to DDM1, so following the results (\cref{thm:ddm1_pd}), this method is coercive.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate thm:sbm_pd (and thm:SBMadv) with the natural energy norm ‖u‖² = ∫_B |∇(φu)|² + ε⁻²(1−φ)u² dx, which is a norm on H¹₀(B) and for which coercivity follows term by term; the advection part of thm:SBMadv is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity guarantee of thm:sbm_pd, and of thm:SBMadv whose proof invokes it for the diffusion part ('Coerciveness has already been shown for the diffusion term in thm:sbm_pd'), is unreliable as stated.
issues.title: SBM coercivity (thm:sbm_pd) is claimed with respect to an inequivalent norm and is false as stated
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated and its proof rests on an invalid equivalence of inequivalent norms; the supported repair replaces the norm (the corrected norm no longer controls φ|∇u|², so the stated guarantee content changes and propagates to thm:SBMadv), but it is local, needs no new proof architecture, and leaves a recognizably comparable coercivity result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Multiplying by $\phi$ and substituting \cref{eq:mixed0-strong1} gives a new method

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying −∇·(φDσ) + Dσ·∇φ + (D/ε²)(1−φ)(u−g) = φf by φ and substituting φσ = ∇(φu) − g∇φ yields the penalty term (D/ε²)φ(1−φ)(u−g), not the displayed (D/ε²)(1−φ)²(u−g). The discrepancy is essential: the literal derivation output φ(1−φ) vanishes in the exterior (φ = 0), so the derived method would exert no control on u in B_ext and could not be coercive, whereas thm:mixed0's coercivity proof relies on the un-derived (1−φ)² coefficient for exterior control (∫_{B_ext}(D/ε²)u²). The claimed derivation therefore does not produce the method analysed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the derivation (e.g., do not multiply the penalty term by φ, or explicitly present (D/ε²)(1−φ)²(u−g) as a modelling choice replacing the derived φ(1−φ) coefficient), keeping meth:mixed0 and thm:mixed0 as stated.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation narrative of the central new method Mix0DDM (and, by template, the rationale for its stabilising structure) is unsupported; the method itself, as defined by meth:mixed0, is unaffected.
issues.title: Mix0DDM derivation produces a φ(1−φ) penalty, not the (1−φ)² penalty actually used
issues.why_classification: The method and its coercivity theorem are stated and proven independently of the flawed algebraic step; a local correction of the derivation (or an explicit statement of the coefficient choice) repairs it with no loss of mathematical content.

issues.failure_explanation: The advection and mass terms of a(u,u) reduce to ∫_B [φ b·∇φ − φ[b·∇φ]⁻ + φm − ½φ²∇·b]u² dx. The proof supports the m/∇·b part only by 'φ² < φ' together with the true but insufficient inequality ∫φ²(m − ½∇·b)u² ≥ 0; the needed inequality ∫(φm − ½φ²∇·b)u² ≥ 0 requires φm ≥ φ²m, i.e. the unstated hypothesis m ≥ 0, which (eq:advCoercive) does not imply. Counterexample within the stated hypotheses: planar interface, b = (0, d·x₂) with d = ∇·b < 0 (so b·∇φ ≡ 0 and the stabiliser −φ[b·∇φ]⁻ vanishes), m = d/2 (so m − ½∇·b = 0), and |d| > 2D/ε²; for u constant on a thin strip where φ ≈ 1−γ (γ small), a(u,u) ≈ c²|S|γ[D/ε²(1 + 81γ) − |d|/2] < 0, so the bilinear form is indefinite. Hence thm:mixed1adv is false as stated (thm:ddm1adv, thm:SBMadv, thm:mixed0adv do not share this defect, since their mass terms enter as φ(m − ½∇·b) or φ²(m − ½∇·b)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis m ≥ 0 (or ∇·b ≥ 0, or a smallness bound on |[∇·b]⁻| relative to D/ε²) to thm:mixed1adv; with m ≥ 0 the existing proof is valid. All applications in the paper (m = 0 or m = 3/(2τ) > 0) remain covered.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity guarantee of thm:mixed1adv, and the claim that meth:mixed1adv's stabilising term yields 'a stable scheme', are unreliable for data with m < 0 even when (eq:advCoercive) holds.
issues.title: Mix1DDM with advection (thm:mixed1adv) is not coercive under the stated hypotheses; the proof needs m ≥ 0
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false in a subregime of its advertised hypotheses, as a concrete counterexample shows; the least repair adds a standard local condition (m ≥ 0) that preserves every application in the paper, but it excludes a data regime the theorem claims to cover — a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: due to the boundary conditions being included in $\sigma \approx \nabla u$

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims E_{H¹} = ‖χ_Ω(u − u_h)‖_{H¹} and, for Mix0DDM and Mix1DDM, computes it as E_{L²} + ‖χ_Ω(∇u − σ_h)‖_{L²}. But σ_h is never defined: the mixed methods (meth:mixed0, meth:mixed1 and their advection versions) are scalar primal formulations for u alone and produce no discrete flux. The H¹ errors and EOCs reported for the mixed methods — including the headline claim that Mix0DDM performs significantly better in the H¹ error — therefore rest on an unspecified quantity, and the displayed equality with the H¹ norm also fails for the plain sum as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define σ_h explicitly for the mixed methods (e.g., via the discrete analogue of φσ = ∇(φu) − g∇φ on Ω, or by stating which post-processed gradient the code uses) and replace the plain sum by the H¹-norm combination; the reported numbers then correspond to a stated quantity.
issues.overall_effect: The reported H¹ errors and EOCs for Mix0DDM/Mix1DDM, and all comparisons based on them, cannot be reproduced or interpreted from the source.
issues.title: H¹ errors for the mixed methods are defined via an undefined discrete flux σ_h
issues.why_classification: A local definitional addition plus a routine norm correction restores well-definedness of the reported metrics; no formal result, method, or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: For −∇·(D∇p) = f with ∇p·n = p_N and n the outward normal (the paper's standing convention, cf. (eq:normal) and the divergence-term derivation just below, which correctly uses n·δ ≈ −∇φ), integration by parts gives ∫_B φD∇p·∇v = ∫_B φfv + ∫_B D·p_N|∇φ|v, so the strong form is −∇·(φD∇p) = φf + D·p_N|∇φ|, i.e. the p_N term enters with a minus sign on the left and with the factor D. The displayed (eq:DDNeumann) has +p_N|∇φ| on the left and no D, so it is not the diffuse-domain approximation of the stated Neumann problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct (eq:DDNeumann) to −∇·(φD∇p) − D·p_N|∇φ| = φf (or state explicitly the sign convention for p_N under which the displayed form holds).
issues.overall_effect: The recalled Neumann DDM approximation is incorrect as displayed; within the paper it is used only with homogeneous data (p_N = 0, 'the term disappears'), so no downstream result is affected.
issues.title: Diffuse-domain Neumann formula (eq:DDNeumann) has the wrong sign and drops the factor D
issues.why_classification: A local sign/factor correction to a recalled background formula that is never used with non-homogeneous Neumann data; no result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which will extend to remove the cylinder from the mesh

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims C_d, C_l are obtained from (2/(ρLU²_mean))∫_{∂Ω}(ν∇u − pI)n dS and its diffuse counterpart ∫_B(pI − ν∇u)∇φ dx. Drag and lift are components of the fluid force on the cylinder, i.e. stress integrals over the cylinder surface only; ∂Ω also contains the no-slip walls and the inflow boundary, whose shear and pressure contributions change the value. With n the outward normal of the fluid domain, both displayed integrals equal minus the standard force on the cylinder, whereas the reported values (C_{d,max} ≈ 2.74–3.08 against the reference 2.95) follow the standard positive convention. Moreover, since only the cylinder is diffuse, ∇φ is supported near the cylinder, so the diffuse integral approximates the cylinder-only integral and the claimed equivalence between the two displayed formulas also fails. The formulas thus do not define the quantities reported in tab:nscoef.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the stress integral to the cylinder surface Γ_cyl (the diffuse version already does this implicitly) and fix the orientation/sign so that C_d and C_l match the benchmark convention of the cited reference values.
issues.overall_effect: The stated definitions of the benchmark quantities of interest (drag, lift) are incorrect; the comparison against reference values in tab:nscoef relies on computations not specified by the displayed formulas.
issues.title: Drag/lift coefficient formulas integrate the stress over the whole boundary and carry the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to the displayed definitions of the measured quantities; the reported drag values match the reference sign and magnitude, indicating the computation used the correct cylinder-only integral, so a local correction of the formulas restores consistency without affecting results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To make this method coercive, so we add the term

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion asserts Mix0DDM was 'the only method proven to be coercive without an additional stabilisation term'. The body establishes the opposite for Mix0DDM: the term (D/4)|∇φ|²(u−g)v (eq:mixed0-stabterm) is introduced precisely 'to make this method coercive', and thm:mixed0 proves coercivity of the stabilised method. Furthermore, DDM1 (thm:ddm1_pd) is coercive with no terms beyond its B.C. penalty, so Mix0DDM is not the only such method under any reading except the advection-stabilisation reading (thm:mixed0adv needs no inflow term), which the sentence does not state.

failure_location.quote: \MixedZ{} method was the only method proven to be coercive without an additional stabilisation term

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to the true statement, e.g. 'Mix0DDM was the only method whose advection terms are coercive without an additional inflow stabilisation term'.
issues.overall_effect: Misleading summary of what was proven about the stabilisation requirements of the new methods.
issues.title: Conclusion falsely states Mix0DDM was proven coercive without a stabilisation term
issues.why_classification: A local wording correction of a summary sentence; no formal result, method, or computation is affected.
